title: Made-to-measure cutting boards
description: A solid wood cutting board made for your worktop: dimensions, wood, stop edge and details agreed personally with Edle Hölzer.
intro: Your worktop. Your dimensions. We make solid wood boards around the way you cook, the space available and the character of your kitchen.
imageAlt: A completed large oak cutting board with a stop edge

sections.title: Made for real kitchens
sections.text: Our completed projects are starting points, not a fixed catalogue of sizes. Oak and Yellow Poplar show how different woods can change the appearance of a substantial board. We choose suitable timber together, based on use, budget and availability.
sections.more: A custom board does not have to be XXL. We can also discuss a smaller serving board, matching breakfast boards for your family or a holder made for a board you already own. Tell us what you want to use it for before deciding on the details.

sections.title: Dimensions, material and handling
sections.text: Measure the usable worktop, including the space you need around the board. Consider the sink, hob, cupboards and where you will lift or store it. Thickness, construction and wood affect the weight as well as the appearance.
sections.more: We discuss edge grain or end grain, rounded or bevelled edges, grip recesses, a stop edge and a juice groove where suitable. Engraving needs a position that works with the design and leaves the working area practical. Not every combination is sensible; we will say so openly.

sections.title: A realistic price framework
sections.text: Depending on size and specification, custom pieces can start at a few hundred euros. We calculate your board individually; there is no universal price per centimetre.
sections.more: Our 75 × 60 cm XXL reference board with a stop edge starts at €1,199 and can reach around €1,600–1,700 depending on specification. This is an upper-range example, not a minimum budget or the quoted price of the photographed customer projects.

sections.title: From first idea to your finished board
sections.text: Send your intended use and any rough dimensions. We discuss feasibility, wood, a price range and production time. We make the agreed design only after your approval.
sections.more: A kitchen photo can help, but you do not need one for the first enquiry. If you are unsure about wood or construction, leave those choices open. We agree collection or dispatch as part of the project; a custom build does not automatically have the dispatch time of a ready-made product.

faq: Can I order any size?
We check whether the proposed dimensions, thickness and construction are suitable. Available timber, stability, weight and everyday handling all matter.
Can you add a juice groove or engraving?
Yes, where the board and intended use allow it. We agree the position and design before production.
Does an enquiry place an order?
No. We first discuss your idea, feasibility, budget and timing. Production requires your approval.

title: Wooden spatulas
description: Handcrafted solid wood spatulas with a personal choice of grain, optional engraving and care advice from Edle Hölzer.
intro: A simple kitchen tool with its own grain and feel. Our solid wood spatulas are made for turning, moving and serving food in everyday cooking.
imageAlt: A solid wood spatula used in a frying pan

sections.title: Choose the wood and your favourite piece
sections.text: Depending on the current selection, we make spatulas from oak, walnut, ash, beech, chestnut, Kambala or Wenge. The orderable woods and edge shapes are shown in the Etsy listing.
sections.more: If several pieces of your chosen wood are available, we can send photos so you can choose your favourite grain. Optional engraving is discussed individually, with a mock-up before it is made.

sections.title: A considered tool for your pan
sections.text: A wooden spatula works without a metal edge against the pan. Smoothly finished surfaces and a length of around 30 cm give it a comfortable feel and keep your hand away from the hot pan.
sections.more: Use it without unnecessary pressure, including on coated pans. Check edges regularly for rough spots. Wood is a solid material, not a flexible plastic blade, and should not be used as a lever.

sections.title: Clean briefly. Let it dry freely.
sections.text: Wash by hand after cooking, wipe dry and allow air to circulate around the tool. Do not put it in the dishwasher or leave it soaking.
sections.more: If the surface begins to feel dry or rough, suitable wood care can refresh it. Our care guide explains cleaning, drying and applying a thin coat without leaving excess on the surface.

sections.title: Build a small, useful kitchen collection
sections.text: Pair a spatula with a wooden dough scraper or butter knife in a complementary wood. Start with tools you will actually use rather than collecting unnecessary accessories.

faq: Can I choose an individual spatula?
If more than one example of a wood is available, ask us for photos before dispatch.
Is it dishwasher safe?
No. Brief hand washing, drying with a cloth and free air drying are the appropriate routine.
Are all woods always available?
No. Check the current Etsy listing for the woods and versions available to order.

title: Cutting boards with engraving
description: Personal engraving on a handcrafted wooden cutting board: choose a clear motif and agree the position with Edle Hölzer before production.
intro: A name, a date or a clear motif can turn a useful board into a personal gift. We help you find a position that belongs on the board, not in the way of using it.
imageAlt: A wooden cutting board with a personal engraving along the edge
cta: Find a board for my engraving

sections.title: Keep the message clear
sections.text: Short names, dates, lettering and simple motifs usually work best. Light wood often makes an engraving more visible than dark or strongly figured timber.
sections.more: Tell us the occasion and the result you have in mind. For business logos, the clarity of the artwork and the available space matter more than the number of details. We check whether a motif is suitable instead of promising that every file will work.

sections.title: Choose the position together
sections.text: An edge, corner, handle area, underside or dedicated serving area may suit the design. The right position depends on the board and its intended use.
sections.more: An engraving in a frequently used cutting area will be exposed to knife marks. A juice groove and engraving also need space to coexist. We discuss these details and provide a mock-up before making the engraving.

sections.title: A personal detail, not a separate product
sections.text: Choose your board first, then agree the engraving. Cutting-board engraving costs €10; the available options are shown on the relevant product page.
sections.more: For dough scrapers, spatulas and butter knives, send your text or artwork and discuss it with us. The product photos show examples; they are not a promise that every layout suits every piece.

sections.title: From idea to approval
sections.text: Send your chosen product and wording or motif. We discuss legibility and placement, prepare the mock-up and make the engraving after you approve it.

faq: Can every board be engraved?
In principle we can engrave wooden boards, but we check the material, available space, motif and intended use first.
Can you engrave a company logo?
Yes, if the artwork and scale are suitable. We discuss the layout before making it.
Is a bigger engraving better?
Not necessarily. A clear, well-positioned engraving often fits a board better than a large design in the working area.

title: Quality wooden kitchen accessories
description: Solid wood boards, spatulas, dough scrapers and care products: a small, useful kitchen collection made by Edle Hölzer in Central Hesse.
intro: Fewer accessories. More substance. A good kitchen collection starts with useful tools, a pleasant feel and materials you enjoy using every day.
imageAlt: A wooden spatula in use while cooking

sections.title: Start with what you use daily
sections.text: A substantial cutting board provides a working surface. A smaller snack board serves breakfast or an evening meal. A spatula turns food, while a dough scraper gathers chopped ingredients or handles dough.
sections.more: Choose a juice groove if you regularly work with juicy food and the board is suitable. It is an option with a purpose, not a detail every board needs. Size, weight and available storage should guide your choice.

sections.title: Quality is more than the name of the wood
sections.text: Look at the surface, edges, joints and handling. A tool should feel comfortable, have a suitable construction and fit the work it is meant to do.
sections.more: Colour and grain make each piece individual, but they do not replace careful workmanship. We select timber and check the finished pieces in our workshop. If you are unsure, we can help you compare suitable products.

sections.title: Care belongs to the collection
sections.text: Wash wooden tools by hand, wipe them dry and let air circulate around them. Appropriate care refreshes a dry surface and supports long-term use.
sections.more: Our care balm combines linseed-oil varnish and regional beeswax. Check the individual product page for its price and what is included; not every board or accessory automatically includes a tin.

sections.title: A gift that has a place in the kitchen
sections.text: Choose a familiar daily ritual rather than an anonymous decorative object. A board, dough scraper or spatula can be personalised with an individually agreed engraving.

faq: Which accessories are useful?
Start with your cooking habits: a suitable board and one or two tools you will regularly use.
Do wooden tools need complicated care?
No. Hand washing, drying and occasional suitable surface care are the essentials. Avoid the dishwasher and prolonged soaking.
Can I combine matching woods?
Yes, subject to the current selection. We can help you choose complementary pieces.

title: Walnut cutting boards
description: Choose a walnut cutting board by grain, construction, weight and intended use, with personal advice from the Edle Hölzer workshop.
intro: Dark heartwood, individual grain and a warm feel. Walnut is a considered choice for a board that remains visible in the kitchen and is used every day.
imageAlt: Walnut cutting boards with different colours and grain patterns

sections.title: Choose more than a colour
sections.text: Grain, surface, weight and size all influence how a walnut board feels in everyday use. A compact board that is easy to lift serves a different purpose from a heavy board that stays on the worktop.
sections.more: For our pure walnut boards, we select the darker heartwood. Natural differences in colour and grain remain part of the material. A photograph represents an individual piece, not a uniform industrial colour.

sections.title: Working board or serving board?
sections.text: Both are possible, but the useful format may differ. Cutting needs enough clear working area; serving also depends on what you will carry, arrange and place on the table.
sections.more: Think about where the board will live and whether you need to move it often. A dark walnut surface creates contrast on a light worktop and can sit quietly alongside darker cabinetry. Judge the whole piece, not only the wood species.

sections.title: Walnut or oak?
sections.text: In our experience, oak is more resistant to visible use marks than walnut. Walnut is softer, so its surface can show use sooner. Both can be good everyday boards.
sections.more: Do not decide on hardness alone. Your knives, preferred feel, kitchen design, the board's weight and your care routine also matter. We help you compare actual pieces rather than treating a hardness number as a complete buying guide.

sections.title: End grain or edge grain?
sections.text: Construction changes the visible grain and the character of the working surface. Compare the available formats and their weight as well as their appearance.
sections.more: A larger end-grain block may suit a permanent preparation area. A smaller edge-grain board can be easier to lift and put away. Neither description alone tells you whether a board fits your kitchen.

sections.title: Care with a light hand
sections.text: Clean briefly by hand, dry with a cloth and let both sides release moisture. Apply suitable care thinly and remove excess rather than leaving a glossy layer.
sections.more: Wood moves as moisture changes. Avoid prolonged soaking, dishwashers and drying against strong heat. If a board needs more than routine care, ask us whether refurbishment is appropriate for its condition.

faq: Is walnut suitable for daily cutting?
Yes, when construction, dimensions and care suit the intended use. Expect natural signs of use rather than an untouched decorative surface.
Is walnut harder than oak?
No. In our workshop experience, oak is more resistant to visible marks. The choice should also consider feel, weight and appearance.
Why do walnut boards look different?
Natural colour and grain vary between pieces. Wood selection and construction also affect the finished appearance.

title: BBQ gifts and Pitmaster Boards
description: A solid wood Pitmaster Board for carving, resting and serving: choose a useful BBQ gift with personal advice from Edle Hölzer.
intro: Made for the moment after the grill. A solid wood Pitmaster Board gives carving, arranging and serving a proper place at the table.
imageAlt: Steak served on a wooden board as a BBQ gift

sections.title: Choose for the food and the cook
sections.text: A steak lover, smoker owner and host preparing food for a group do not necessarily need the same board. Match the working area to the food and leave enough room for carving and serving.
sections.more: Large cuts can benefit from a substantial surface, but a board that is difficult to carry or wash may be the wrong gift. Consider worktop space, weight, grip and where it will be stored.

sections.title: What makes a useful Pitmaster Board?
sections.text: A stable working surface, appropriate dimensions and comfortable handling matter more than decorative extras. A juice groove can help with juicy food where the board is suitable.
sections.more: We discuss a surrounding groove or an additional collecting basin when appropriate. A large format alone does not make a board better; construction, thickness and the way it is used need to work together.

sections.title: A personal detail for a real occasion
sections.text: A name, date or restrained motif can make a BBQ board a personal birthday, wedding or housewarming gift. We agree the engraving position before it is made.
sections.more: Keep the main cutting area usable and allow space for any groove. If a standard format does not suit the recipient's grill station or kitchen island, we can discuss a made-to-measure board.

sections.title: A gift made to be used
sections.text: Wood will show use. A thoughtful gift includes an understanding of cleaning, drying and care, rather than an expectation that the board must remain untouched.

faq: What size should a BBQ board be?
Choose around the food, available worktop, handling and cleaning space. We can advise on a suitable existing or custom format.
Can it be engraved?
Yes, subject to the board and motif. We agree a position that works with the working area and any juice groove.
Does every BBQ board need a juice groove?
No. It depends on the food and intended use. We recommend it only where it makes sense for the board.

title: Thoughtful gifts made from wood
description: Handcrafted wooden gifts for daily rituals: cutting boards, kitchen tools and personal engraving from Edle Hölzer in Central Hesse.
intro: A gift becomes personal when it belongs to someone's everyday life. Start with the person, the occasion and the way the piece will be used.
imageAlt: A wooden cutting board presented with care balm and a care guide

sections.title: Choose a ritual, not just an object
sections.text: Breakfast, baking, preparing dinner and sharing food each suggest different pieces. A butter knife or dough scraper can be as thoughtful as a large board if it fits the recipient.
sections.more: Consider space, weight and how often the piece will be used. A serving board suits a different routine from a permanently placed chopping block. We can help you choose within your budget.

sections.title: A shared design for the family
sections.text: Matching breakfast boards or complementary kitchen tools can connect individual gifts without making every piece identical. Natural grain still gives each one its own character.
sections.more: We discuss wood, format and personal details together. Availability can vary, so a photo selection is useful where several individual pieces are in stock.

sections.title: Personalise with care
sections.text: An individually agreed engraving can add a name, date or short message. We prepare a mock-up before making it and choose a position that suits the product.
sections.more: For company gifts, quantity, budget per piece and timing are important from the start. Our dedicated corporate page provides an enquiry route for that discussion.

sections.title: Know what comes with the gift
sections.text: The specific product page lists the contents. Extra pieces or care products shown in a photograph are not automatically included with every product.
sections.more: Tell us if you would like to combine items. We agree the actual pieces and presentation rather than treating a sample photograph as a universal set.

faq: Can a wooden gift be personalised?
Yes, where the piece and motif are suitable. We agree the engraving with you before production.
Do you offer gifts for businesses?
Yes. Tell us the quantity, budget and occasion through our corporate gifts page.
How should the recipient care for it?
Hand wash, dry and allow air to circulate. Follow the care guidance for the specific product.

title: Press and people behind Edle Hölzer
description: Meet Özgür and Serkan Koç and the Edle Hölzer workshop in Central Hesse. Background, craft, materials and contact for press enquiries.
intro: Edle Hölzer is a small woodcraft workshop in Central Hesse. We make boards and kitchen tools with individual grain, direct personal advice and a focus on keeping good pieces in use.
imageAlt: Özgür working at the table saw in the Edle Hölzer workshop

sections.title: Özgür: design, timber and craftsmanship
sections.text: Özgür Koç founded Edle Hölzer and has worked in skilled crafts for around 20 years. He is responsible for design, wood selection and production.
sections.more: The boards are traditionally worked by hand, deliberately without CNC. The material, intended use, edges, surface and handling are considered together rather than judged by wood species alone.

sections.title: Serkan: making the details visible
sections.text: Serkan Koç is an engineer and amateur photographer, responsible for the online presence. Through photography and video he brings the craft, materials and details of the work into view.

sections.title: Stories from the workshop
sections.text: Care instead of disposal, choosing material for a purpose and working with historic timber are recurring themes. The numbered Erbstück series gives selected old wood another role.
sections.more: Not every old beam is suitable for a cutting board. We assess the substance, cracks and grain before deciding whether to make a piece. Existing traces can remain part of its character; suitability comes first.

sections.title: A digital space for personal advice
sections.text: The website helps people compare formats, learn about care and consider a board in their own kitchen. Custom projects begin with a conversation about use, dimensions and budget.
sections.more: For press, collaborations, workshop photography or questions about a specific piece, please contact us. Image use and publication rights must be agreed; photographs on the website are not a blanket licence to reuse them.
